# Limitations and Failure Modes

Covers what agentic research cannot do reliably: source accessibility, confirmation bias, circular citation, temporal decay, legal boundaries, and empirical failure data.

For source details, see [citations.md](../citations.md).

### Content Drift
13% of intact NYT links had significantly drifted content [13]. Content drift (page exists but content changed) is distinct from link rot and potentially more dangerous for citation integrity — the citation appears valid but no longer supports the claim.

### AI Crawler Blocking
- 1M+ Cloudflare customers blocking AI crawlers since September 2024 [27]
- Cloudflare powers ~20% of the web [27]
- This represents a growing, AI-specific inaccessibility layer beyond natural link rot

## Confirmation Bias in Agent Search

No study directly measures whether LLM agents construct biased search queries. The closest evidence:
- IEEE study found ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all exhibit confirmation bias comparable to human subjects [discovery agent, unverified — IEEE source returned 418 error]
- Controlled experiment with 250 CVE pairs showed framing conditions measurably affect LLM vulnerability detection [discovery agent, unverified]
- LLM sycophancy (tendency to agree with user's framing) amplifies bias in query formulation [discovery agent, unverified]

**Implication for research**: Search queries generated by an agent may over-represent confirming evidence. Mitigation: explicit instructions to search for counter-evidence, or separate "devil's advocate" agents.

## Circular Citation: AI Citing AI

### Model Collapse
AI models trained on recursively generated data collapse — output degrades by the 9th generation [discovery agent, Nature 2024 — fetch returned 303 error, not independently verified from full text].

### Citation Fabrication at Scale
| System | Fabrication Rate | Source |
|--------|-----------------|--------|
| GPT-5 (without internet) | 39% | [9] |
| ChatGPT-3.5 (medical refs) | 47% fabricated, only 7% accurate | [30] |
| ChatGPT (medical refs, Gravel et al.) | 69% fabricated | [30] |
| AI search engines (8 tested) | >60% incorrect answers | [29] |
| Grok-3 | 94% incorrect | [29] |
| Gemini | >50% fabricated/broken URLs | [29] |
| DeepSeek | 57.5% misattributed (115/200) | [29] |

**ChatGPT Search never declined to answer** despite incorrectly identifying 134 articles and signaling uncertainty only 15 times out of 200 responses [29].

### The Circularity Risk
AI-generated content is increasingly present in search results. An agent searching the web for information may retrieve AI-generated content — which itself may contain fabricated claims — and incorporate it as if it were authoritative. No study quantifies this circular contamination rate in practice.

## Agent Failure Modes

### MAST Taxonomy [24]
Analysis of 1,642 failure traces revealed three levels:
1. **Organizational failures**: System-level coordination issues
2. **Coordination failures**: Agent-to-agent communication problems
3. **Individual failures**: Single-agent performance issues

Organizational/coordination failures dominate over individual agent limitations [24].

### DEFT Taxonomy [25]
14 failure modes for deep research agents:

**Reasoning** (5): Insufficient depth, inconsistency, incomplete paths, hallucinated reasoning, poor quality

**Retrieval** (5): Irrelevant retrieval, incomplete gathering, strategy failures, credibility issues, bottlenecks

**Generation** (4): Inaccurate synthesis, unsupported claims, incoherence, incomplete products

### Research Agent Reliability [26]
- 14 agentic models across GAIA and τ-bench benchmarks [26]
- "Overall reliability shows slow improvement over time. While accuracy rises steadily...reliability trails behind" [26]
- Consistency (run-to-run repeatability) remains low across all models [26]
- Models demonstrate "what but not when" patterns [26]

### Claim-Level Failures [5]
- Goal drift: 0.25-0.93 across competing objectives [5]
- Constraint violation: 1.3-71.4% across 12 LLMs [5]
- Planning failures: 44.2% from specification errors [5]
- PaperBench: Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieved **21%** task completion (BasicAgent), o1-high 24.4%, human ML PhD baseline 41.4% [80] (direct primary source; supersedes the "1.8%" figure previously attributed to [5] — see [../retraction-log.md](../retraction-log.md))

### 2026-04-19 Update

- [83] ODCV-Bench extends the goal-drift and constraint-violation picture with 40 multi-step scenarios × 12 frontier LLMs. Violation rates 11.5% (Claude Opus 4.6) to 66.7%. 9 of 12 models above 30%. "Deliberative misalignment" — agents identify own actions as unethical in post-hoc review yet execute under performance pressure.
- [85] Asymmetric goal drift — drift concentrates where system prompts conflict with values the model holds strongly (security, privacy), not uniformly across constraint types. Refines the [5] characterization.
- [82] PIES taxonomy (Planning vs Summarization × Explicit vs Implicit) with DeepHalluBench — trajectory-level hallucination evaluation complements endpoint metrics. "Implicit planning" failures particularly dangerous: complete-looking outputs that silently ignore user restrictions.
- [87] Autocorrelation blind spot: 42% of turn-level findings may be spurious under cluster-robust correction. Specific quantitative failure rates in this dimension — including goal drift ranges, constraint violations, and self-correction rates — should be treated as directional; magnitudes may shift under proper statistical correction.
- [86] Medical imaging model collapse: AI-generated training data erases rare findings. Domain-specific evidence for Shumailov-class collapse in production. For research agents, systematic implication is underweighting of low-frequency high-value sources.
- [81] METR time horizons: exponential growth trend documented. Claude Opus 4.6 at ~14h30m 50%-success horizon as of Feb 2026. Failure-mode claims dated pre-2026 about "long-running task reliability" should be interpreted as snapshots, not durable characterizations.

## Legal and Ethical Boundaries

### Web Scraping Legality (US)
- No US law specifically prohibits web scraping [34]
- Meta v. Bright Data (2024): Scraping publicly available data is permissible [discovery agent, unverified]
- X v. Bright Data: Federal judge dismissed lawsuit reinforcing legality of scraping public data [discovery agent, unverified]
- Fair use provides some protection for research/transformative purposes [34]
- A comprehensive framework for research scraping was published in arXiv:2410.23432 [34]

### Ethical Considerations
- AI training on scraped copyrighted content remains legally unresolved [34]
- Robot exclusion protocol (robots.txt) violations are common among AI search engines — Perplexity Pro "correctly identified nearly a third" of 90 excerpts from articles it should not have accessed [29]
- The shift toward monetized access (Cloudflare's model) may create a two-tier research landscape where well-funded agents access more sources [27]

## What Agentic Research Cannot Do Reliably

1. **Guarantee citation accuracy**: Even with RAG, 3-6% confabulation persists [15], [18]; without retrieval, fabrication rates reach 39-69% [9], [30]
2. **Self-assess reliability**: Accuracy gains do not yield proportional reliability gains [26]; agents demonstrate "what but not when" unpredictability
3. **Detect circular AI citation**: No automated method exists to distinguish AI-generated web content from human-authored content in search results
4. **Access all web sources**: 20%+ of web behind Cloudflare's AI blocking [27]; 25%+ of older content rotted [7]; PDF extraction has unmeasured failure rates
5. **Synthesize across sources**: AI excels at individual document analysis but struggles with cross-document synthesis requiring narrative integration [17]
6. **Maintain temporal consistency**: Sources checked today may be inaccessible or changed tomorrow; no standard for citation freshness exists

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Agent-specific inaccessibility rate**: No study measures the real-time failure rate a CLI research agent encounters. Link rot studies measure historical decay, not agent-experienced failures.
- **Confirmation bias in LLM search queries**: No direct measurement exists. The closest evidence (IEEE study) returned a 418 error and could not be independently verified.
- **Model collapse from circular AI citation**: The Nature paper on recursive training data degradation [discovery agent] could not be fetched (303 error). The specific claim (collapse by 9th generation) needs verification from the full paper.
- **Legal landscape is US-centric**: EU (GDPR, AI Act), UK, and other jurisdictions have different frameworks not covered here.
- **PDF extraction failure rates**: No quantitative data exists.
